prompt: A survey of $200$ customers gives a $95\%$ confidence interval for a proportion with margin of error $0.06$. The manager wants a margin of error of $0.03$ at the same confidence level, and expects $\hat{p}$ to stay about the same. About how many customers should the new survey include?
hint: Margin of error is proportional to $\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$ — not $\frac{1}{n}$.

hints.text: Margin of error is proportional to $\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$ — not $\frac{1}{n}$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: going from $n = 100$ to $n = 400$ doubles $\sqrt{n}$ from 10 to 20, so the margin of error halves. Multiply $n$ by 4 to halve the margin.
Halving ME needs $\sqrt{n}$ to double, so $n$ must be multiplied by $2^2 = 4$.

explanation: ME $= z^* \sqrt{\hat{p}(1-\hat{p})/n}$. With $z^*$ and $\hat{p}$ fixed, ME $\propto 1/\sqrt{n}$.
To cut ME from $0.06$ to $0.03$ (half), $\sqrt{n}$ must double, so $n$ must quadruple.
New sample size: $4 \times 200 = 800$. Doubling to 400 would only shrink the margin to about $0.042$.
